title: Hydrostatic generating functionals and derivative-expansion boundaries

items.title: Static hydrostatic background and equation-of-state data
items.physical_scope: Prescribed smooth static SI background and pressure data only; no equilibrium-state existence, microscopic trace, convergence, or empirical assertion.
items.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty compact smooth three-manifold without boundary, let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and give $M=\mathbb R\times\Sigma$ the product smooth structure. Write $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$ for the standard length coordinate on $\mathbb R$ and use spatial coordinates measured in metres. For a smooth function $N:\Sigma\to(0,\infty)$, extend $N$ constantly along $\mathbb R$ and define the metric on $M$ by $g=-N^2\,dx^0\otimes dx^0+h$, where $h$ is pulled back from $\Sigma$. The metric components and lapse $N$ are dimensionless in these length coordinates. This is a static spacetime model: the coefficients are independent of $x^0$, $\partial_{x^0}$ is the selected future timelike Killing field, and $N$ is its lapse, so $g(\partial_{x^0},\partial_{x^0})=-N^2$.

The Riemannian volume density of $h$ is denoted by $dV_h$; in length coordinates it has units of cubic metres and finite total volume, and no orientation of $\Sigma$ is required. In a fixed SI gauge, let $\Phi:\Sigma\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth electrostatic scalar potential in volts, let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a fixed charge in coulombs, let $T_0>0$ be a reference temperature in kelvins, and let $\mu_0\in\mathbb R$ be a reference chemical-potential parameter in joules. The sign convention is that the local electrochemical parameter is $\mu_0-q\Phi$. For the static Killing field $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$, its lapse is $N_\xi=N$; fix the Killing-normalized temperature $T_K:=N_\xi T$ to be the constant $T_0$, so the local temperature is $T(x)=T_0/N(x)$. Define the local chemical-potential field by $\mu(x)=(\mu_0-q\Phi(x))/N(x)$ for $x\in\Sigma$; then $q\Phi$ and $\mu$ have units of joules.

Let $D\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be an open domain for the pair $(T,\mu)$, measured in kelvins and joules, and let $p:D\to\mathbb R$ be a supplied $C^2$ pressure function with values in pascals. Require $(T(x),\mu(x))\in D$ at every $x\in\Sigma$. The function $p$ is model input; this definition does not derive an equation of state or assert that the prescribed data have a material realization.

references.title: Nabamita Banerjee et al., Constraints on Fluid Dynamics from Equilibrium Partition Functions, arXiv:1203.3544v2, §§1.1–1.2 and 2.3.1 (2012)

items.title: Restricted hydrostatic effective functional
items.physical_scope: An adopted zeroth-gradient effective equilibrium functional on a compact smooth static background in a declared long-wavelength regime; no microscopic trace, convergence, empirical equation of state, or transport coefficient is asserted.
items.statement:
Use the prescribed static hydrostatic data $\Sigma,h,N,\Phi,q,T_0,\mu_0,D,p,dV_h$, with local profiles $T=T_0/N$ and $\mu=(\mu_0-q\Phi)/N$. Fix the background fields and parameters, and take an open interval $U\subset\mathbb R$ containing $\mu_0$ such that $(T_0/N(x),(r-q\Phi(x))/N(x))\in D$ for every $r\in U$ and $x\in\Sigma$. Adopt the dimensionless effective functional

$$W_{\rm hs}(T_0,r;h,N,\Phi,q,p):=\log Z_{\rm eff}=\frac{1}{k_BT_0}\int_\Sigma N(x)\,p\!\left(\frac{T_0}{N(x)},\frac{r-q\Phi(x)}{N(x)}\right)dV_h(x),$$

with the integral finite. Here $Z_{\rm eff}:=\exp(W_{\rm hs})$ is notation for the adopted functional; no microscopic trace or Gibbs state is asserted. “Hydrostatic” labels this prescribed static equilibrium response model: the background is time-independent along the chosen Killing field and the Killing-normalized temperature is $T_0$; it does not assert a fluid-equation solution or a thermal state. A “derivative expansion” means a formal ordering of candidate corrections by the number of derivatives of the prescribed background and local thermodynamic variables; this postulate retains its order-zero term only. Each application declares a microscopic length $\ell_{\rm micro}>0$ in metres, a microscopic relaxation time $\tau_{\rm micro}>0$ in seconds, and a positive spatial background scale $L_{\rm bg}$ in metres, identifying the physical meaning of each without equating distinct microscopic scales; $L_{\rm bg}$ is the shortest declared spatial variation or curvature scale among the prescribed fields. The static model is used only in the declared spatial long-wavelength regime $\ell_{\rm micro}/L_{\rm bg}\ll1$. Its integral contains no temporal gradients; any time-dependent extension must separately declare a temporal variation scale $t_{\rm bg}>0$ in seconds and satisfy $\tau_{\rm micro}/t_{\rm bg}\ll1$. No numerical error bound, convergence of a gradient expansion, or microscopic existence claim is asserted. The pressure function $p(T,\mu)$ is separately supplied and is not identified with a pressure derived from a material energy function unless an application states that additional equation-of-state identification.

references.title: Nabamita Banerjee et al., Constraints on Fluid Dynamics from Equilibrium Partition Functions, arXiv:1203.3544v2, §§1.1–1.2, 2.3.1, and 2.5 (2012)
Pavel Kovtun, Lectures on hydrodynamic fluctuations in relativistic theories, complete lecture notes, §§1.3 and 2.6 (2012)

items.title: Hydrostatic susceptibility and Tolman variables
items.physical_scope: Conditional derivative identity and nonnegativity of the model chemical-potential response in the compact smooth static-background functional; no trace, microscopic existence, convergence, or empirical conclusion.
items.statement:
Fix the background data $\Sigma,h,N,\Phi,q,T_0,p$ of the adopted compact hydrostatic functional and vary only its chemical-potential parameter $\mu_0$ inside the open interval $U$ specified by that model. The local temperature profile $T=T_0/N$ has constant Killing-normalized value $NT=T_0$; this is the model's Tolman profile. Write $p_\mu$ and $p_{\mu\mu}$ for the first and second derivatives of the pressure function with respect to its chemical-potential argument, evaluated at $(T_0/N(x),(\mu_0-q\Phi(x))/N(x))$. Then

$$\partial_{\mu_0}W_{\rm hs}=\int_\Sigma\frac{p_\mu(T_0/N,(\mu_0-q\Phi)/N)}{k_BT_0}\,dV_h,\qquad \partial_{\mu_0}^2W_{\rm hs}=\int_\Sigma\frac{p_{\mu\mu}(T_0/N,(\mu_0-q\Phi)/N)}{N k_BT_0}\,dV_h.$$

The model chemical-potential susceptibility $\chi_{\rm hs}:=\partial_{\mu_0}^2W_{\rm hs}$ is nonnegative if $p_{\mu\mu}(T_0/N(x),(\mu_0-q\Phi(x))/N(x))\ge0$ for every $x\in\Sigma$. With the stated SI conventions, $W_{\rm hs}$ is dimensionless and $\chi_{\rm hs}$ has units $\mathrm{J^{-2}}$. This is a deduction inside the adopted effective model, not an empirical charge-fluctuation claim.

references.title: Nabamita Banerjee et al., Constraints on Fluid Dynamics from Equilibrium Partition Functions, arXiv:1203.3544v2, §§1.1, 2.3.1, and 2.5 (2012)

title: Hydrostatic generating functionals and derivative-expansion boundaries — Examples

items.title: Equilibrium functional supplies no transport coefficient
items.physical_scope: Conditional comparison of two constitutive model instances sharing one hydrostatic pressure functional; no solution existence, empirical response, or universal transport claim.
items.statement: Suppose an application supplies a shared thermodynamic state map on which the pressure in the static hydrostatic functional equals the equilibrium pressure used by the local dissipative constitutive branch. At a common admissible local input with nonzero expansion $\theta$, fix any $\zeta_*>0$ in pascal-seconds and compare two model instances that agree on all hydrostatic data and use constant bulk-viscosity coefficients $\zeta_1=\zeta_*$ and $\zeta_2=2\zeta_*$. The bulk-viscosity coefficient here is the coefficient $\zeta$ multiplying the expansion in $\Pi=-\zeta c\theta$; $\theta=\nabla_a u^a$ is the expansion of the stated observer field. Their adopted hydrostatic functionals are identical, while their bulk-pressure corrections differ by $\Pi_2-\Pi_1=-\zeta_*c\theta\ne0$. This difference has units of pressure. Thus hydrostatic data alone do not fix the bulk viscosity. This is a conditional comparison of constitutive maps; it asserts neither a solution of the balance equations nor an empirical response.

references.title: Nabamita Banerjee et al., Constraints on Fluid Dynamics from Equilibrium Partition Functions, arXiv:1203.3544v2, §§1.1–1.2 (2012)
Pavel Kovtun, Lectures on hydrodynamic fluctuations in relativistic theories, complete lecture notes, §§1.3 and 3.2 (2012)
